headline: Fractions are the mathematics of sharing—expressing parts of wholes with precision
universal_truth: Everything can be divided; understanding the parts reveals the nature of the whole
fun_facts: Ancient Egyptians only used unit fractions—fractions with 1 on top, like 1/2, 1/3, 1/4
The fraction bar (the line between numbers) was invented by Arab mathematicians around 1200 CE
Fractions can describe probabilities, ratios, rates, and proportions—not just 'pieces of pie'
discussion_questions: When do you use fractions in everyday life?
Why are some fractions harder to visualize than others?
How do fractions help us be more precise than whole numbers?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Half a pizza. A quarter of an hour. Two-thirds of the vote. We constantly work with parts of things, not just whole things. Fractions are how we express these parts precisely—the mathematics of 'some but not all.'

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Fractions seem simple—just two numbers with a line between them. But why do we need both numbers? What does each part of a fraction actually tell us?
cliff.prompt: What do the two numbers in a fraction represent?

options.text: The bottom says how many equal parts make the whole; the top says how many parts we have
options.response: Yes. Denominator defines the partition; numerator counts the pieces. Together, they pinpoint a value.

options.text: The top is always smaller than the bottom to show it's less than one
options.response: Often true, but 'improper' fractions like 5/4 exceed one...

q1.title: Egyptian Origins
q1.script: Ancient Egyptians used fractions 4,000 years ago—but only 'unit fractions' with 1 on top. To express 2/3, they'd write 1/2 plus 1/6. Our modern fraction notation took millennia to develop.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Egyptian Origins"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: More Than Pie
q2.script: Fractions aren't just for dividing pizzas. They express probabilities—1 in 4 chance. Ratios—3 parts flour to 2 parts water. Rates—miles per hour. The same notation describes many different relationships.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Infinite Precision
q3.script: Between any two whole numbers are infinite fractions. Between 0 and 1 alone: 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 2/3, 3/4, 7/16... Fractions reveal that the number line is infinitely dense. There's always a number between any two numbers.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Understanding parts reveals the nature of wholes. Fractions teach precision—not just 'some' but 'exactly how much.' In life, vague answers often hide in fractions waiting to be specified.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 101—we're into triple digits now! Tomorrow, we'll discover another way to write fractions—decimals. Until then, notice the fractions hiding in your day.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Fraction Awareness - Find the Parts
growTrack.activity: Today, notice when you encounter fractions: splitting bills, measuring ingredients, calculating discounts, estimating time. How often do you think in parts rather than wholes? Fractions are everywhere once you look.
